Your mission

We're looking for product-minded engineers to join our diverse and driven team. We really value collaboration, making an impact, and continuous learning. Our product development team is based in Berlin, but we have folks working all over Europe, and you'll work closely with an experienced and supportive team.


Your profile

We are looking for a Senior Fullstack Engineer with deep expertise in Go to join a diverse, product-minded team that values collaboration, impact, and continuous learning. 

We're a distributed engineering team working across Europe (within +/- 1 hour of CET); topi is headquartered in Berlin. Engineers are expected to be comfortable navigating the entire stack (both Frontend and Backend).

In this role, you will be architecting features from the database to the browser. Your center of gravity is the Go backend, APIs, data models, system design, but you'll move into the React/TypeScript frontend whenever the feature requires it. You'll join an experienced and supportive team where you'll have a significant voice in shaping both our technical direction and the product itself.
     About You
This is a role for an engineer who lives in the backend but enjoys reaching across the stack. You'll thrive here if you can:

  • Own the Full Lifecycle: Build, scale, and maintain modern web applications where the heavy lifting sits in our Go backend, with the willingness to ship in React/TypeScript on the frontend whenever a feature calls for it.    
  • Bridge the Gap: Design and implement clean APIs in Go while ensuring they are seamlessly integrated into a performant, accessible React frontend.
  • Architect for Scale: Maintain high standards for code quality and performance across the entire stack, from backend microservices to frontend component libraries.
  • Collaborate Broadly: Work closely with Product and Design to turn ambiguous requirements into polished features.
  • Agentic Engineering Mindset: You treat AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, and the like) as real collaborators, not autocomplete. You own every line that ships under your name, whether you typed it or an agent did. You're motivated to deep-dive into agent workflows and bring the judgment that turns agent output into production-grade code.

To Be Successful in This Role, You'll Need:
  • Experience: at least 6+ years of professional software engineering experience in a production environment.
  • The Backend: Proven experience architecting and maintaining high-scale web APIs. You've shipped Go in production for 2+ years and are comfortable owning backend system design end-to-end.
  • The Frontend: Motivated and willing to work in our React/TypeScript frontend, with enough baseline ability to ship features there when a story calls for it. Prior hands-on React/TypeScript experience is a plus, not a must.
  • System Ownership: A "DevOps" mindset, comfortable with CI/CD, automated testing, and version control.
  • Communication: Fluent English and the ability to explain complex technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders.
What we care about
  • Teamwork: collaborating and supporting each other within engineering and across functions
  • Inclusion: creating an environment where everybody can bring their whole self and do their best work
  • Ownership: empowering you to do the work that is most impactful
  • Sustainability: balancing work with family and personal hobbies so we can be at our best
  • Growth: supporting each other's learning and development


Why topi?

  • Impact from Day One - Your ideas are valued, and you actively shape our direction. No long feedback loops or complex hierarchies - you'll have a direct impact on what you do.
  • Trust - We believe in our mission and in our team, offering trust-based working hours, permanent contracts, flexibility for home-country working.

Talent Acquisition Specialist (m/f/d) | Elternzeitvertretung / Parental Leave Cover
Fixed-term, around12 months  |  ideally part-time (60–80%), with the option to extend to full-time  |  Berlin (hybrid)  |  Recruiting for SRLabs and Allurity group companies
based candidates.

Please apply only if you are based in Berlin and has right to work. No visa sponsor available, No remote options available.

About us
SRLabs is home to some of the sharpest minds in cybersecurity. We secure critical infrastructures in finance, energy, and telecommunications — not through compliance checklists, but through hands-on hacking resilience. Our work lives at the intersection of deep technical research and impactful consulting for organisations that care about staying ahead of real threats.
We're a team of 60 people based in Berlin, with colleagues from all over the world. We're part of Allurity, a European cybersecurity group of 12+ sister companies, which gives us scale without sacrificing our startup energy.

We're looking for a Talent Acquisition Specialist to cover a parental leave for around 12 months. In this role, you won't just recruit for SRLabs — you'll also support hiring across several of our Allurity sister companies, working closely with our cross-company People Hub. It's a great opportunity to get hands-on, end-to-end recruiting experience across a range of technical and business roles, in an organisation that takes hiring seriously without drowning it in process.


Your responsibilities

Full-Cycle Recruiting

  • Own end-to-end recruiting for open roles at SRLabs and selected Allurity sister companies — from intake call to signed offer.
  • Write and post compelling, accurate job ads that speak to the kind of people we want to attract.
  • Screen applications and conduct first-round interviews, giving candidates a fair, fast, and human process.
  • Coordinate interview loops with hiring managers and technical interviewers, and keep candidates informed at every step.
Sourcing
  • Proactively source candidates for harder-to-fill and technical roles via LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean search, and other channels.
  • Build and maintain talent pipelines for recurring role types across the group.
  • Help identify and test new sourcing channels, particularly for niche cybersecurity talent.
Cross-Company Collaboration
  • Partner with hiring managers and People colleagues across Allurity sister companies to understand their hiring needs and local market context.
  • Contribute to shared recruiting standards, templates, and best practices via the People Hub.
  • Support group-wide initiatives such as the graduate/internship pilot and employer-branding activities where relevant.
Candidate & Hiring Manager Experience
  • Be the main point of contact for candidates throughout the process — approachable, responsive, and clear.
  • Coach hiring managers on structured interviewing and help them make confident, fair decisions.
  • Gather feedback to continuously improve the candidate and hiring manager experience.
Systems & Process
  • Keep our ATS/Personio data accurate and up to date — job postings, pipelines, candidate statuses, and reporting.
  • Maintain recruiting-related documentation and help keep our hiring process easy to follow for everyone involved.
  • Track basic recruiting metrics (time-to-fill, pipeline health, source effectiveness) and flag bottlenecks early.


What do you bring?

  • Proven technical recruiting experience (agency or in-house) — this is a must. You've hired engineers, security specialists, or comparable technical profiles, and you can hold a credible conversation with them. This isn't a role for a first-time recruiter, but you don't need to be senior either.
  • A bit of hands-on sourcing know-how — comfortable using LinkedIn Recruiter or similar tools, and not afraid of a Boolean search string.
  • Good communication skills in both German and English — you can run a candidate conversation and write a clear job ad in either.
  • A structured, organised way of working — you keep pipelines tidy and don't let candidates fall through the cracks.
  • Genuine affinity for tech and cybersecurity talent — you don't need to code yourself, but you understand technical roles well enough to assess and engage the people in them.
  • Comfortable working across multiple companies and stakeholders at once, with a good sense for adapting your approach to different teams and cultures.
  • Ownership mentality — you follow through, flag issues early, and don't wait to be told what's next.
  • Based in Berlin, with an existing right to work in Germany.


What awaits you with us?

  • A front-row seat in the world of cybersecurity — one of the most interesting and relevant fields there is right now.

  • A close-knit, international team that takes the work seriously but doesn't take itself too seriously.

This is a fixed-term position (Elternzeitvertretung) for approximately 12 months, covering a parental leave. It starts as a part-time role at 60–80%, with the option to move to full-time during the contract term depending on hiring volume. There's a real possibility of a handover period with the current role holder to ensure continuity.

Idealworks builds industrial automation as a coordinated system — mobile robots, orchestration software, simulation, and increasingly humanoids and physical AI, working together in real production environments rather than as isolated pilots. Since our founding within BMW Group and our integration into Agile Robots SE, we've grown from a Munich-based robotics team into a global player.

As physical AI and humanoid robotics move from research into industrial deployment, our project landscape is expanding: today's programs span classic mobile robot fleets, next-generation humanoid platforms, and the simulation environments used to develop and validate both. We're looking for a Senior Engineering Project Manager to lead this kind of work end to end - technically credible enough to sit with R&D and hardware/software engineering, and organized enough to keep shareholders, partners, and customers aligned as programs move from concept to production.

data.description:
Material Bank is the world's largest material marketplace for the architecture and design industry. Operating in 37 countries, our platform has become the standard for design professionals around the globe. Every day, Material Bank connects thousands of designers with tens of thousands of materials from leading brands. Material Bank is the fastest and most powerful way for design professionals to search, sample, and specify materials.

Senior Analytics Engineer, Analytics & Insights 

London, UK (Hybrid, 2 days in office) 

Material Bank is the world's largest material marketplace for the architecture and design industry. Operating in 37 countries, our platform has become the standard for design professionals around the globe. Every day, Material Bank connects thousands of designers with tens of thousands of materials from leading brands. Material Bank is the fastest and most powerful way for design professionals to search, sample, and specify materials. 

About the role 

We are looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to join Analytics & Insights, the team that owns Material Bank's analytics data layer, internal reporting, and data products that support our teams and brand partners. 

This is a hands-on technical role for someone who wants to own how analytics get built. You will take approved metric definitions and business questions and turn them into the models and metric logic in Snowflake and dbt, the dashboards, and the semantic layer and data products people use every day. 

You will own the analytics engineering for key areas of the business: understanding what needs to be measured, building the models, validating the logic, delivering the reporting, and keeping it accurate and reliable over time. You will work across multiple departments and across our data products, including embedded analytics for brands. The work varies day to day, and as a team we contribute to everything. 

What we require 

  • Ownership, end to end. You own what you build, from the first stakeholder conversation to the model, the dashboard, and the fix when something breaks. 
  • Precision and attention to detail. You understand the nuance behind a number, verify before you publish, and produce work that leaders and brand partners can trust without checking. 
  • Appetite for hard work. We are a small, ambitious team with a lot of goals. The work is demanding and the hours vary with what needs to get done. We are upfront about that because it is what the role is. 

What you'll do 

  • Own the analytics engineering for assigned business domains, translating metric definition through data model, dashboard, and insight. 
  • Design, build, and maintain documented, production-quality dbt models in Snowflake that turn approved metric definitions into reliable, reusable models and semantic definitions, and power reporting, self-serve, automation, and AI. 
  • Identify and resolve technical inconsistencies in metric logic so the business runs on one certified source of truth. 
  • Build a small set of high-value dashboards in Tableau (and Sigma, as we evolve the stack). 
  • Contribute to the semantic layer so certified metrics are reusable across BI tools, Snowflake Cortex, and embedded analytics. 
  • Automate recurring analytics work, with the tests and monitoring that keep it trustworthy. 
  • Partner with analysts and stakeholders to interpret data, build context, and surface risks before they are asked. 
  • Contribute to brand-facing data products used by account teams and manufacturer partners. 

What you'll bring 

  • 5+ years in analytics engineering, data analytics, or a similar technical analytics role, owning data models and reporting that a business relies on. 
  • Expert SQL on large and complex datasets. You write clean, efficient queries and can debug someone else's logic as easily as your own. 
  • Strong hands-on Snowflake and dbt (or a comparable modern data stack), including dimensional modeling, incremental models, testing, and documentation. 
  • Strong Tableau skills. Sigma, Looker, or similar a plus. 
  • Strong judgment on metric design: grain, denominators, filters, time zones, deduplication, and the ways a correct number can still mislead. 
  • Commercial sense and curiosity. You want to understand why a number matters, can explain what a change means for the business, and hold a position under questioning. 
  • An automation mindset. When you see something repetitive or fragile, your instinct is to find a better way to build it. 
  • Comfort working across several domains at once, prioritizing your own work, and managing stakeholders directly. 
  • Clear, concise communication and the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences. 

Preferred 

Helpful, not required: 

  • Python for automation and data validation 
  • Marketplace, e-commerce, or B2B SaaS analytics 
  • Event and behavioral data (Segment, GA4, or similar) 
  • Semantic layers and AI-assisted analytics (Snowflake Cortex, dbt Semantic Layer, or similar) 
  • Embedded or customer-facing analytics (ClickHouse, Preset, or similar) 
  • Experimentation and causal methods: A/B testing, cohort analysis, difference-in-differences 
  • Catalog, product attribute, or search data 

What success looks like 

In your first 30 days you understand the stack, the models, the people, and the priorities in your domains, and you have your first dbt change merged. 

By 60 days you are producing real work independently: agreed metric definitions implemented, your first certified models and dashboards in use, and a plan for the first manual workflow you will automate. 

By 90 days stakeholders treat you as their analytics partner rather than a request queue. Your models are trusted, your dashboards are used without hand-holding, and your automation is reducing real manual effort. 

This is a senior individual-contributor role with broad ownership and hands-on responsibility. Direct people management is not required. 

What you'll get:

  • Our people: If you thrive in an inclusive, innovative, and fast-paced organization, look no further! You will get to work alongside some of the brightest minds - Join a genuinely fun and supportive workplace where we keep our employees consistently engaged through internal communication and corporate events
    Relaxation and Celebrations: Generous PTO, Paid National Holidays, and even more (ask us about this when we connect).
    Health Benefits: We contribute to your medical healthcare
    rowth: We'll help you take your career to the next level. We want you to be creative and take initiative which will allow you to grow and create within the company. Most importantly, be the best at what matters!
    Flexible Work Schedules: With business units and employees across the globe, Material Technologies has embraced a hybrid working model allowing department leaders to decide on the best approach for their respective teams, whether that be remote, in person, or a little of both.
  • Application Process: Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter outlining their qualifications and relevant experience. We are committed to diversity and encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply. 

Material Bank connects design professionals to hundreds of manufacturers through facilitating brand discovery, sales rep engagement, and material sampling. Our powerful material database and proprietary robotic distribution facility allow members to order samples to be delivered free of charge overnight.Material Bank was founded by Adam Sandow in 2018 and has deeply transformed how the Architecture and Design industry works in the United States. It's an exciting time for the company - Material Bank is growing rapidly and expanding the business to Europe with regional headquarters based in Paris, and offices in London and Stuttgart. Candidates who join us will have the unique opportunity to define, build, and shape our European business.

Material Bank uses your information to process your current application and offer you job opportunities in the future. You have the right to access, rectify, and erase this information, as well as to limit its use or object to it and give directives on its fate after your death. For more information, please consult our privacy policy: https://www.materialbank.eu/privacy-policy

 

What you'll get from us:

  • Our people: We are a growth-driven team that values efficiency, builds smart automation, operates in small empowered teams, and moves quickly from idea to execution.
  • Relaxation and Celebrations: Flexible PTO, Sick Days, Paid National Holidays, and even more (ask us about this when we connect). 
  • Health Benefits: We contribute to your medical, dental, vision and short-term/long-term disability plans and have a strong employee assistance program.

  • Flexible Work Schedules: With business units and employees across the globe, Material Technologies has embraced a hybrid  working model allowing department leaders to decide on the best approach for their respective teams, whether that be remote, in person, or a little of both.

Role: Regional Operations Director (EMEA)

Location: London, United Kingdom (3 days a week from our London offices)

About the role: 

The Regional Operations Director is accountable for the operational effectiveness of the EMEA region. Reporting to the Global Chief Transformation and Operations Officer, you'll translate the global operating model into practical, market-specific execution — building the structure, governance and performance focus needed to strengthen operational control and support scalable growth.

You'll lead a regional operations team, partner closely with regional and global leadership, and act as the key connector between regional execution and global capability. The role calls for a leader equally comfortable setting strategic direction and solving complex operational problems hands-on — someone who turns data into action, builds high-performing teams, and keeps commercial performance firmly in focus.

What you will be doing: 

 

Regional operational leadership

  • Set clear priorities, accountabilities and ways of working for the EMEA Regional Operations function.
  • Build the structure, rhythm and capability needed to improve client delivery, business performance and regional growth.
  • Act as the senior operational partner to Regional Leadership on risks, performance, capacity and improvement priorities.

Client delivery operations

  • Own the operational run model for EMEA clients — including cadence, governance, issue resolution and escalation management.
  • Partner with Account Leadership to ensure delivery risks are visible, blockers are resolved quickly and client teams are set up to deliver effectively.
  • Ensure regional clients are mobilised and supported through consistent operating standards and reliable delivery controls.

Governance, cadence and decision management

  • Own the regional governance rhythm: forums, communications, decision-making and performance reviews.
  • Ensure decisions are made at the right level, escalations are routed effectively and regional context is represented in relevant global and regional forums.
  • Drive clear actions, accountability and follow-through across the function.

Operating model execution

  • Embed the global operating model across EMEA, ensuring standards, processes, tools and governance expectations are adopted consistently.
  • Translate enterprise-level standards into practical, market-specific ways of working.

About Deliveroo

Our mission is to transform the way people shop and eat, bringing the neighbourhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops and riders. We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of one of the most rapidly expanding industries in the world: a complex, always-on, three-sided marketplace that impacts millions of people every day.

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

The Team

BizOps is the team that keeps its finger on the pulse of business performance: continuously, rigorously, and across multiple dimensions at once. We turn raw operational and financial data into actionable intelligence, surfacing what is happening, why it is happening, and what to expect next, for the operators, executives, and functional teams who run the business day to day.

We are not a reporting function that produces outputs on request. We work continuously, proactively watching, delivering, and questioning whether the signal is real, acting as "first responders" to surprising deviations from expectation and using what we learn to drive faster, better decision-making for the business at large.

Our work spans the full stack of analytics: from the warehouse models that make metrics trustworthy, to the monitoring systems that catch problems early, to the reports and dashboards that make performance visible, to the deep-dive investigations that explain what the numbers mean and what we should do about it.

We anchor our analysis to the right reference points: how performance compares to plan, to prior periods, and to what we'd expect, and we bring causal rigour when the business needs to know whether an action actually worked.

The culture within the team is informal, fast-paced and entrepreneurial. Given the growth of the business and the level of senior stakeholder exposure, progression in the team can be fast.

The Role

Deliveroo is hiring a Senior Data Scientist to join BizOps, based in our London HQ (hybrid, minimum three days per week in the office).

This role is largely project-based: starting from a strategic or performance question, you'll combine data, business context, and structured problem-solving to provide the insights that drive decision-making at a global level with senior stakeholders. You will own delivery end-to-end, from the messy, ambiguous question to a rigorous, trustworthy, and actionable answer.

You'll be equally comfortable building the systems that make performance visible and going deep on the investigations that explain it. One week you might diagnose why a key market has moved away from plan; the next, identify the drivers behind a change in customer or operational performance; the next, build monitoring that helps teams spot and understand emerging issues earlier.

Success in this role requires building effective working relationships across Deliveroo, particularly with international markets, as well as the Data Science, Operations, Commercial, and Finance teams.

 

What You'll Be Doing

  • Answer the questions that matter, continuously. Maintain a rigorous view on business performance: Are we on track against our goals? What's changed? How does this compare with what we expected? What should we expect next? Then go further: Why is it happening, what matters most, and what should we do about it?"

  • Own delivery end-to-end. Independently identify, define, and deliver impactful work aligned with business goals, operating with minimal guidance to ship fast, high-quality solutions.

  • Navigate ambiguity. Deconstruct broad, ambiguous problem spaces into structured analytical roadmaps, and understand how your work intersects with adjacent systems and teams.

  • Build for scale, not one-offs. Build the pipelines, models, dashboards, monitoring, and investigative tooling that make performance visible and reliable. Automate wherever possible; redoing analyses by hand is slow and error-prone.

  • Measure impact with discipline. Design measurement strategies from simple A/B tests to quasi-experimental designs (synthetic control, difference-in-differences, event studies) when trials aren't feasible, always with conservative, assumption-explicit language.

  • Be a first responder. Surface deviations before they become escalations, and be just as willing to give the confident "this is noise, no action needed" as the alarm.

  • Communicate to influence. Translate complex findings into clear, simple, actionable recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences that shape roadmaps and decisions.

  • Raise the bar. Contribute to the broader Analytics community, improve shared approaches and best practices, and help build data literacy across the business.

What You'll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate brings strong expertise in some of these areas and the curiosity to grow in others:

  • Experience in an analytical or data science role, such as data analytics, data science, forecasting, planning, strategy analytics, or a similar discipline. Experience in logistics, e-commerce, marketplaces, or another fast-moving, customer-focused business is useful but not essential.

  • Proficiency with SQL and a scripting language such as Python or R, alongside experience with BI or visualisation tooling such as Looker, Tableau, or similar.

  • Comfortable using modern AI-assisted tools to work efficiently while maintaining high standards of accuracy and reproducibility.

  • A pragmatic approach to problem-solving: you can balance analytical rigour with speed, adapt your approach to the importance of the decision, and focus effort where it will have the greatest impact.

  • Effective problem-solving: you can take an ambiguous question, identify the underlying problem or decision, develop hypotheses, and use data and business context to reach a clear point of view.

  • Experience with experimentation and/or causal inference is a strong plus: the ability to unpick insights and steer strategic decisions.

  • Excellent communication skills, in person, in writing, and in code, with the ability to translate business needs into analytical problems and complex findings into simple recommendations.

  • Driven, hard-working, and agile. BizOps sits at the centre of a fast-growing business; we move quickly to scale at pace.

  • London-based, with a minimum of three days per week in the office.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving.

About the team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. OpenAI for Government (OAI4G) helps public-sector institutions understand, adopt, and deploy highly capable AI products in support of their missions. The team brings together Sales, Solutions, Partnerships, Technical Success, Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, and other cross-functional partners to help governments use AI responsibly and effectively.

As part of OAI4G’s International Public Sector team, you will help public institutions in the UK, Middle East (ME) and Latin America (LATAM) translate frontier AI into secure, compliant, mission-aligned outcomes. We work across varied procurement, regulatory, security, sovereignty, and commercial environments, while maintaining a consistent commitment to safety, reliability, and public benefit.

About the role

We are seeking a Global Account Director (GAD) to lead OpenAI’s public-sector work across the UK, ME and LATAM. You will build trusted relationships with government leaders, develop and execute account strategies, create and close complex opportunities, and help customers move from initial interest to successful adoption.

This is a full-cycle, highly cross-functional sales role that combines technical understanding, strategic vision, partnership management, and value-driven execution. You will work with senior government, operational, technical, procurement, policy, and security stakeholders to identify high-impact AI use cases and translate them into credible commercial and deployment pathways across the OpenAI Platform API and Codex and ChatGPT Enterprise.

You will also be an accountable customer leader after signature, working alongside specialist delivery and technical teams to keep customer outcomes, milestones, adoption, risks, and executive alignment on track. The role requires excellent judgement, executive presence, local fluency, and the ability to move between strategy, discovery, capture, procurement, delivery governance, and relationship management without day-to-day direction.

This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will

  • Own a focused portfolio of UK, ME and LATAM public-sector accounts.

  • Build and execute comprehensive account plans that map mission priorities, stakeholders, procurement paths, partners, use cases, risks, and long-term expansion opportunities.

  • Drive complex opportunities through the full sales cycle, from pipeline generation, discovery, qualification, capture, and commercial strategy through negotiation, closure, adoption, and expansion.

  • Lead public-sector customers through their AI adoption journey, helping them identify responsible, high-impact use cases and connect mission outcomes to OpenAI’s capabilities and limitations.

  • Translate between government leaders, end users, technical teams, policy and security stakeholders, and internal product and engineering partners, clearly communicating requirements, progress, risks, and dependencies.

  • Serve as the accountable customer lead for engagements tied to clear outcomes, customer milestones, adoption measures, and commercial commitments, coordinating closely with technical specialists.

  • Work closely with the Partnerships team, global and regional system integrators, cloud and technology providers, local delivery partners, resellers, and strategic international partners to shape joint pursuits, deployment models, and purchasing paths.

  • Develop capture strategies, competitive positioning, win themes, teaming decisions, and proposal narratives that reflect UK, ME and LATAM market conditions.

  • Navigate public-sector procurement, tendering, security, data-residency, compliance, and sovereignty requirements, bringing Legal, Security, Policy, Global Affairs, Finance, and other partners into opportunities early.

  • Build trusted relationships with senior government executives and decision-makers, while staying close to operational users and technical stakeholders whose workflows determine successful adoption.

  • Maintain accurate pipeline, forecasting, account records, customer follow-up, and executive reporting, with disciplined follow-through across markets and time zones.

  • Monitor the government, technology, procurement, partner, and competitive landscape across UK, ME and LATAM markets, surfacing insights that inform product roadmaps and go-to-market strategy.

  • Represent OpenAI at government, partner, and industry forums, strengthening networks and identifying opportunities that advance responsible public-sector adoption of AI.


We’re seeking someone with experience including

  • 10+ years in government, diplomacy, national security, international development, multilateral institutions, public-sector technology sales, business development, consulting, transformation, systems integration, or a closely related field, with meaningful ownership of complex customer outcomes.

  • Direct experience in government, diplomacy, national security, foreign affairs, or international organisations, or very significant experience working with those customers in sensitive, regulated, or high-consequence environments.

  • Material experience operating credibly in sensitive or national-security-adjacent settings; an active or recently held government security clearance is valuable, and the ability to obtain or maintain any clearance required for the portfolio may be necessary.

  • A strong record of shaping and closing complex cross-border deals: account planning, discovery, qualification, stakeholder mapping, capture, proposal development, negotiations, forecasting, closure, adoption, and expansion.

  • Executive presence with senior diplomats, ministers, multilateral executives, government leaders, and decision-makers, alongside credibility with technical, operational, procurement, policy, and security stakeholders.

  • Sound understanding of multilateral and public-sector procurement, funding, contracting, security, privacy, data-residency, sovereignty, and compliance requirements across more than one ME or LATAM market.

  • Ability to orchestrate regional and international partners, including system integrators, resellers, cloud providers, development institutions, advisory partners, and delivery partners.

  • Enough AI and enterprise-technology fluency to explain OpenAI’s products, capabilities, limitations, and responsible-use trade-offs clearly to diplomatic, multilateral, and government audiences, and to engage the right specialists early.

  • High ownership, exceptional written and verbal communication, diplomatic judgement under ambiguity, strong capacity management across regions and time zones, and willingness to travel across ME and LATAM, and internationally as needed.

Nice to have

  • Deep relationships across international organisations, regional bodies, development institutions, foreign affairs, defence, national security, or other sensitive public-sector communities.

  • Experience developing opportunities across more than one ME or LATAM market, ideally with exposure to international organisations or regional bodies.

  • Experience with AI/ML, cloud, data platforms, cybersecurity, API-based products, public-sector digital transformation, or regulated cross-border technology deployments.

  • Experience moving a complex cross-border opportunity from early mission discovery through procurement, deployment governance, adoption, and measurable outcomes.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. We are a fast-moving, well-funded company, fresh off a $143M Series C at a $1.5B valuation — building Agentic Change Management, the control layer for software changes created by humans and agents. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck moves from implementation to judgment and helping human judgment scale is exactly the problem we exist to solve.

The Commercial Field Engineer’s primary role is to serve as a technical advisor and champion for CodeRabbit customers in the Commercial tier throughout their post-sales journey. In this function, you will play a crucial role in onboarding, implementation, and ongoing success by partnering with Customer Success, Product, Engineering and Support teams to ensure customers realize the full value of CodeRabbit.

About Airwallex

Airwallex is the only unified payments and financial platform for global businesses. Powered by our unique combination of proprietary infrastructure and software, we empower over 250,000 businesses worldwide – including Brex, Navan, Qantas, SHEIN and many more – with fully integrated solutions to manage everything from business accounts, payments, spend management and treasury, to embedded finance at a global scale.

Proudly founded in Melbourne, we have a team of over 2,300 of the brightest and most innovative people in tech across 27 offices around the globe. Valued at US$11 billion and backed by world-leading investors including T. Rowe Price, Visa, Mastercard, Robinhood Ventures, Sequoia, Salesforce Ventures, DST Global, and Lone Pine Capital, Airwallex is leading the charge in building the global payments and financial platform of the future. If you’re ready to do the most ambitious work of your career, join us.

 

Attributes We Value

We hire successful builders with founder-like energy who want real impact, accelerated learning, and true ownership. You bring strong role-related expertise and sharp thinking, and you’re motivated by our mission and operating principles. You move fast with good judgment, dig deep with curiosity, and make decisions from first principles, balancing speed and rigor.

You're humble and collaborative; turn zero‑to‑one ideas into real products, and you “get stuff done” end-to-end. You use AI to work smarter and solve problems faster. Here, you’ll tackle complex, high‑visibility problems with exceptional teammates and grow your career as we build the future of global banking. If that sounds like you, let’s build what’s next.

 

The Role:

We're looking for a dedicated, organised Senior Complaints Specialist to join us as we build our Complaints function in EMEA from the ground up - this is our first dedicated complaints hire in the region. You'll spend the majority of your time as a proactive, high-energy complaint handler: resolving complex disputes and keeping pace with our regulatory deadlines. This is much more than a standard complaint handler role: alongside resolving complex disputes, you'll lead our monthly complaints reviews, drive root cause analysis, and step up complaints handling processes for the region.

Who you are:

  • You're a natural complaint handler – you take ownership of a steady caseload, resolve issues objectively and fairly, and can turn a messy, technical problem into a clear explanation for the customer. You also have extensive knowledge of UK regulations including DISP and the FOS complaints handling process.

  • You're organised and deadline-driven – you manage your own schedule to make sure every case is resolved within the required legal timeframes, without needing to be chased

  • You're detailed-orientated– you can prepare thorough case files, gather evidence, and represent Airwallex professionally in front of the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • You're ready to step up – you’ll run our monthly complaints meetings and drive root cause analysis across EMEA.

  • You're a great collaborator – you'll work closely with internal teams to fix the root cause of issues.

  • You’re ambitious – you're excited by the idea of shaping how we run complaints across EMEA as our first hire in the function, and by helping us build how we use AI to handle complaints at scale

Responsibilities

  • Manage your caseload: Take ownership of a steady stream of complaints, meeting daily targets while maintaining high standards.

  • Meet regulatory timelines: Manage your own schedule to ensure every case is resolved within the required legal timeframes

  • Lead on regulator escalations: Manage cases that reach the Financial Ombudsman Service, preparing thorough case files, gathering evidence, and drafting Airwallex's final position

  • Own the regulator relationship: Act as the day-to-day point of contact with the Ombudsman, keeping our responses professional, timely and factual

  • Lead our EMEA complaints reviews: Run our monthly complaints meetings, bringing visibility to trends, volumes and priorities across the region

  • Drive root cause analysis: Work cross-functionally with internal teams to identify why issues occur, and lead the push for long-term fixes rather than one-off resolutions

  • Help build our complaints AI capability: As volumes grow, help shape how we use AI to handle complaints more efficiently at scale

What you'll bring:

  • 5+ years' experience handling regulated complaints, ideally within financial services

  • Strong working knowledge of DISP and other relevant complaints-handling regulation

  • Experience preparing cases for, and liaising with, regulators such as the Financial Ombudsman Service

  • A track record of meeting productivity and quality targets in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills in English

  • Experience driving root cause analysis or process improvement cross-functionally

  • Confidence using AI-driven tools to automate manual processes and improve efficiency

  • Fintech or payments experience is required

Applicant Safety Policy: Fraud and Third-Party Recruiters

To protect you from recruitment scams, please be aware that Airwallex will not ask for bank details, sensitive ID numbers (i.e. passport), or any form of payment during the application or interview process. All official communication will come from an @airwallex.com email address. Please apply only through careers.airwallex.com or our official LinkedIn page.

Airwallex does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms/recruiters. Airwallex will not pay any fees to search firms/recruiters if a candidate is submitted by a search firm/recruiter unless an agreement has been entered into with respect to specific open position(s). Search firms/recruiters submitting resumes to Airwallex on an unsolicited basis shall be deemed to accept this condition, regardless of any other provision to the contrary.

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

As Associate Corporate Counsel, you will support Airwallex’s growth in the UK by providing practical, business-focused legal advice on corporate, regulatory and commercial matters. OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice.

By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we’ve transformed how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of Europe’s largest car-changing destinations. Over 10 million customers have used carwow to buy and sell cars, with £3bn worth of cars bought and £1.8bn listed for sale last year alone.

In 2024, we acquired Autovia — creators of Auto Express and evo — doubling our audience overnight. Today, our brands reach over 350 million users annually and generate 1.1bn+ YouTube views, influencing how millions of drivers choose their next car.

And we’re a long way from done.

GYC ADVERTISING @ CARWOW

This role sits within GYC (Get Your Car) Advertising, a fast-growing commercial team responsible for building Carwow’s Used and New Car Advertising business.

The two markets are at very different stages:

  • New Car Advertising is a mature, high-performing product with strong market fit and limited competition.

  • Used Car Advertising is an emerging channel — competitive, fast-moving, and still being proven.

We operate like a startup within a startup:

  • small team

  • high ownership

  • evolving products and processes

  • limited structure by design

As a BDR, you’ll help build the foundations of this business by creating high-quality outbound pipeline, shaping how we approach dealers, and defining what “good” looks like from the ground up.

YOUR MISSION

Your mission is to create qualified pipeline from cold outbound outreach, focused initially on Used Car Advertising, and set the sales team up to win.

This role is not about closing deals or working warm leads.

It’s about discipline, resilience, and learning — building strong sales fundamentals in a fast-moving, high-accountability environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Generate outbound pipeline (Used-first)

  • Cold-call and message independent dealers and retail groups

  • Open relevant commercial conversations about Used Car Advertising

  • Book qualified meetings only for BDMs

Qualify before you book

  • Ask structured discovery questions

  • Understand dealer context (stock size, sales velocity, appetite to invest)

  • Disqualify early when there’s no fit

Build strong sales fundamentals

  • Learn how carwow demand works

  • Develop an understanding of used-car dealer economics

  • Improve messaging and objection handling through repetition and feedback

Operate with discipline

  • Hit clear daily and weekly activity targets

  • Maintain accurate CRM records

  • Protect BDM time by avoiding low-quality meetings

KEY REQUIREMENTS

  • Comfortable with cold outreach and rejection

  • Clear, concise communicator

  • Able to follow structure and process consistently

  • Curious about how businesses make money

  • Coachable and open to feedback

  • Resilient and focused under pressure

BONUS POINTS

  • Previous outbound sales or customer-facing experience

  • Exposure to automotive, marketplaces, or performance-led products

  • Desire to progress into more senior commercial roles over time

WHY THIS MIGHT NOT BE FOR YOU

  • If you’re looking for inbound or warm leads

  • If you dislike repetition and outbound activity

  • If you prefer closing over qualifying

  • If you need heavy structure and certainty from day one

FINAL NOTE

This role is ideal if you want to learn outbound sales properly, build real commercial skills, and progress over time into broader Used and New Car Advertising roles.

If you’re resilient, curious, and ready to build from scratch, we’d love to talk.

About Sona

Running a frontline business is an operational puzzle most software has never touched. Shift-by-shift labour costs, compliance that changes by region and by role, and margins thin enough that a badly built rota can sink a quarter. It's a harder problem than most white-collar SaaS, and yet frontline sectors employ 80% of the global workforce and have received about 1% of the last decade's software investment.

We think that's because the problem needed AI, not just better software, before it was solvable. Frontline organisations sit on enormous amounts of operational data. Used properly, that data lets agents take on real parts of running the business rather than just reporting on it. That's what we're building at Sona, and it's early enough that the systems you build now will still be foundational in three years.

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

About the Role

Sona's Labour AI team builds the forecasting, rules and scheduling tools that help hospitality and retail businesses get staffing right. Getting the tooling built is one problem. Getting it to actually work for a specific site, with its own trading patterns, staff and quirks, is another. That's what this role owns; working directly with customers to turn Sona's forecasting and scheduling tools into labour models that actually get used on site.

You'll derive labour rules from real trading data, spend time on site with customer teams to learn how the business actually runs, and build the trust with site managers that makes a new workload model stick. You'll present the impact and ROI of that work to customer executives and general managers, and act as the subject matter expert for labour optimisation in sales conversations.

You'll also be the person site managers trust enough to change how they staff, and the person customer executives and General Managers trust enough to back the changes you're proposing. That's an influence job as much as an analytical one. You'll report back to customer leadership on the impact, in numbers they can take to their own board.

There's no fixed playbook here. You'll adapt the same underlying labour model across different business types, from QSR to premium dining to retail.

Responsibilities

  • Derive labour rules from real trading data using Sona's tooling and your own operational knowledge

  • Spend time on site with customer teams, learning practical realities like stock deliveries and close-down procedures

  • Build trust with site managers so workload models actually get followed

  • Present impact and ROI to customer executives and general managers, winning buy-in for operational change

  • Act as the labour optimisation subject matter expert in sales conversations

  • Work across the full portfolio of live customer projects, picking up work as priorities shift between accounts

Requirements

  • Comfortable with technology and confident picking up new tools quickly, including using AI tools in your own workflow

  • Comfortable operating without a fixed playbook

  • Excited about using AI in your day-to-day work to 10x your output

Hello there. We’re Zopa.
 
We started our journey back in 2005, building the first ever peer-to-peer lending company. Fast forward to 2020 and we launched Zopa Bank. Our vision for a new era of banking puts people front and centre — we’ve built a business that empowers everyone to aim high, every day, to move finance forward.   • Customer impact over unnecessary complexity

    Zopa is proud to offer a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and backgrounds leads to better products for our customers and a unique company culture for our people. We are made up of nearly 50 nationalities, have a DE&I forum made up of Zopians wanting to make a difference and we are proud of our culture where everyone can bring their full self to work. Our approach to DE&I is reflected in our hiring process so please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments. 
     

    Our approach to AI in interviews

    At Zopa, AI isn't something we're testing out — it's part of how we work every day. As a proud partner of Jobs 2030, we're committed to building AI fluency across our workforce, and we expect Zopians to use AI as part of how they do their jobs.

    Behavioural and competency-based interviews: please don't use AI. These conversations are designed to understand you — your experiences, your judgment, and how you've approached real situations. An AI-generated answer can't tell us that. What it can do is get in the way of us finding out whether we're the right fit for each other. 

    Technical interviews: it depends on the role. Some technical stages actively welcome AI use, others don't. Your Talent Partner will let you know what's expected at each stage. Where AI is part of the assessment, we'll be interested not just in the outcome, but in how you used it – the tools you chose, your reasoning, and the decisions you made along the way.

Mission

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear.

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose

As Regional Operator Education Specialist you are responsible for the quality and delivery of onboarding for clinical operators across your region, ensuring training maintains a consistently high standard. You support and quality-assure the work carried out by Clinic Trainers, and act as the escalation point for clinical training matters, so that methods, delivery, and assessments stay aligned with global standards.

You also contribute to the maintenance of training programs and content, adapting them for local market needs based on central guidelines and frameworks. This is a competency-based training and safety function.

A note on this role

Medical Education at Neko is growing and its structure is still developing. This is an interim appointment, and the scope described here may change as the wider function takes shape. We will be open with you about any changes as they happen.

What You'll Deliver

Onboarding quality and escalation

  • Ensure clinical operator onboarding is delivered to a high and consistent standard across your region, aligned with central guidelines and member safety requirements.

  • Run the onboarding cycle: confirm incoming starters with Recruitment, allocate trainers, and monitor daily trainee progress, stepping in early where progression is slow.

  • Hold the decision to pass, extend, or offboard a trainee in your region, alongside the Lead Operator team.

  • Act as the regional escalation point for clinical training quality and safety matters, triaging every case on first pass to distinguish a genuine safety risk from a standard performance gap, and seeing it through to closure including structured improvement plans.

Support and coach Clinic Trainers

  • Provide guidance, feedback, and support to Clinic Trainers on training methodology, delivery, and assessment.

  • Hold trainers in your region to one national standard, working with Lead Operators so operational needs are met at the same time.

  • Follow up on trainer performance and development.

  • Support Clinic Trainers in completing Impact Reviews for existing clinical staff in line with Neko’s pillars.

Maintain and adapt training programs

  • Maintain training programs and materials as requested, including Sana content, and adapt them to local market needs while staying aligned with global standards and following approval guidelines.

  • Work from one shared source with your counterpart region rather than maintaining separate regional versions, and flag content gaps and inconsistencies centrally rather than resolving them locally in isolation.

  • Deliver or coordinate key clinical skills training within your region, for example Gen II retrofit training, and provide training-plan input into clinic launches and retrofits.

Monitor training quality and drive improvement

  • Observe training delivery, provide structured feedback, and follow up on what changes as a result.

  • Run regional training audits and benchmarks against the national standard, identifying gaps and putting forward improvement proposals, including corrective action where an audit finding requires it.

  • Oversee trainers’ records of staff competency sign-off. No operator works unsupervised on a new device until sign-off is confirmed.

  • Feed hiring and training trends back to Recruitment so screening improves from what is seen downstream in training.

Partner across the business

  • Work closely with clinic leadership and relevant support functions so training meets operational needs as well as the clinical standard, and act as a regional training voice with Recruitment, clinic leads, and cluster management, syncing regularly to stay aligned nationally.

  • Work closely with Clinical Development, participating in product launch handovers and acting as the educational link for your region, including developing training materials for new devices and SOPs when requested and supporting rollout to trainers and operators on the ground.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Healthcare professional with at least two years of clinical experience.

  • Significant post-registration experience in a fast-paced, high-volume clinical setting.

  • Demonstrated clinical leadership, formal or informal.

  • Existing trainer or competency sign-off experience within a Neko clinic, or equivalent clinical procedure competency such as phlebotomy or ECG.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing clinical teams or trainers, including performance management across multiple sites.

  • Track record in competency-based training and assessment.

  • Experience developing or scaling training frameworks to support clinic expansion.

  • Cross-functional collaboration with Recruitment, Operations, or Education teams.

  • A postgraduate certification in a specialist clinical area or in leadership.

Key competencies

  • Strong communication and a coaching mindset

  • Sound clinical judgement under ambiguity

  • A collaborative approach with operators, clinic leads, and trainers

  • Adaptability to new processes and policies

  • Attention to detail in competency checks and training materials

  • Organisational skills across multiple concurrent onboarding cycles

  • A proactive, problem-solving approach to gaps in knowledge or process

Working conditions

  • This role carries protected training capacity on a fixed weekly structure, with a minimum of one scanning day so you remain clinically current and credible with the operators you train.

  • A minimum trial or shadow period applies before full sign-off authority is confirmed, given the clinical safety responsibilities of the role.

  • This is a hands-on regional role with regular travel across your clinic cluster.

The Role 

As Head of Product, you are the voice, validator and external face of QUOODA. Engineering owns what gets built and why; you bring the customer and commercial judgement they need to make those decisions well, and you are accountable for ensuring the product meets the bar before it reaches customers. Day to day, your closest working relationships are with the CTO and Director of Engineering: you keep them unblocked, informed and well-connected to the commercial and customer context they need. You are the product's spokesperson externally to customers, to sales and new business, and to customer success and you facilitate a direct, unfiltered relationship between engineering and the wider business. You do not sit in the middle: you remove friction, surface context, and validate outcomes. 

 

Key Responsibilities 

 

Product direction and voice 

  • Set and communicate product strategy. Curate and communicate the QUOODA v2 roadmap, reflecting engineering decisions and ensuring the rationale is clearly articulated to the business and market. 
  • Be the spokesperson for QUOODA. Represent the product internally and externally through demos, briefings, webinars, customer councils, sales conversations and analyst or prospect engagements. 
  • Work closely with the CTO and Director of Engineering. Be their primary point of contact for commercial and customer context. Keep them informed of business priorities, market signals and customer feedback so they can make well-grounded decisions without being pulled into business-facing meetings themselves. Flag blockers, misalignments and communication gaps early. 
  • Facilitate prioritisation. Facilitate prioritisation conversations between engineering, commercial and customers. Bring domain and customer context to those decisions, and ensure engineering has what it needs to make well-informed calls. 

Commercial, customer success and sales partnership 

  • Enable sales and new business. Equip the commercial team with messaging, positioning, demo narratives and answers to the hard questions, so they can win against incumbents and triple our customer base by 2030. 
  • Partner with customer success. Translate adoption signals, support themes and renewal risk into product decisions, and give CS the roadmap clarity they need to retain and grow accounts. 

The v1-to-v2 migration 

  • Support engineering in leading the migration of 70 customers from QUOODA v1 to v2. Own the customer-facing communication and experience of the migration. Be the named, accountable point of contact for customers throughout the transition, ensuring engineering has the business and customer context needed to sequence and execute it well. 
  • Surface migration risk to engineering. Ensure engineering has unfiltered customer insight to inform their parity decisions. Own the customer-facing communication of each change — what is different, why, and what support is available, once engineering has made those calls. 
  • Lead the UAT process for QUOODA v2. Be the primary voice from the customer and business perspective on whether the product is ready. Sign off that it meets the bar commercially and functionally in partnership with engineering who hold the technical quality bar. The go/no-go decision is a shared call, and it is explicit. 
  • Curate the backlog of known issues. Turn five years of accumulated, hard-won knowledge about v1's gaps into clear intent for v2. 

Working in an AI-native SDLC 

  • Surface context, not tickets. Surface customer problems, commercial outcomes and real-world constraints in a form that is immediately useful to engineers and AI agents. The goal is to enrich engineering's intent, not to originate it. 
  • Represent the product-engineering model externally. Help customers, partners and the wider business understand how our product-engineering model works and why it produces better outcomes. Engineering owns the operating model itself; your role is to make it legible and credible to the outside world. 

 

Requirements  

 

Essential 

  • Demonstrable product leadership experience in B2B / enterprise SaaS, ideally with a complex, configurable platform. 
  • A credible, confident external presence, comfortable being the face of a product with customers, prospects, sales and CS. 
  • Strong commercial instinct: you understand how product decisions drive pipeline, win rates, retention and growth. 
  • Experience owning a major product transition, migration or re-platforming with a live customer base. 
  • Fluency with (or genuine enthusiasm to embrace) an AI-native, agentic software development lifecycle: working alongside AI coding agents, expressing intent rather than writing exhaustive specs, and evaluating AI-built software. 

 

Highly desirable 

  • Regulated domain experience, ideally in GRC, risk, compliance, audit, or adjacent regulated enterprise software. 
  • Familiarity with API-first, cloud-native product architectures. 
  • Hands-on comfort with AI tooling: prototyping, prompting, and defining evaluations to assess output quality. 
  • Experience in a private-equity backed or high-growth scale-up environment. 

 

Benefits 

  • Competitive salary (depending on experience). 
  • 25 days annual leave (excluding UK bank holidays). 
  • 5% Matched company pension. 
  • Vitality private health insurance (includes Vitality membership). 
  • 4x salary life cover. 
  • Perk Pal retail discounts. 
  • Regular virtual and in-person social events. 

 

If you are a strategic thinker with a passion for writing high-scale, secure, cloud native software, this is an exciting opportunity to grow and help shape the future of our product, platform, and culture.  

 

Sustainware is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Established in 2004, OLIVER is the world's first and only specialist in designing, building, and running bespoke in-house agencies and marketing ecosystems for brands. We partner with over 300 clients in 40+ countries and counting. Our unique model drives creativity and efficiency, allowing us to deliver tailored solutions that resonate deeply with audiences. 

As a part of The Brandtech Group, we're at the forefront of leveraging cutting-edge AI technology to revolutionise how we create and deliver work. Our AI solutions enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results. 

Role: Design Director (part time - 2.5 days a week)

Location: London/Hybrid with occasional travel to Birmingham 

About the role: 

As Design Director, you'll serve as both brand guardian and strategic creative partner for Client — leading the studio's creative output while building close relationships with senior stakeholders across marketing, communications, and the partnership. This is a director-level role with genuine scope: you'll set the creative vision, maintain brand consistency across all channels, and develop the talent around you. You'll work closely with OLIVER's creative leadership, bringing your expertise to everything from campaign concepting and typographic craft to team coaching and executive presentations.

What you will be doing: 

 

  • Lead all visual communications for Client, acting as brand guardian across print, digital, social, and events — ensuring consistency, quality, and strategic alignment at every touchpoint
  • Set the creative vision and direction for the studio, translating complex briefs from senior stakeholders into compelling, sophisticated design solutions
  • Build, mentor, and develop the in-house creative team — providing clear creative direction, constructive feedback, and ongoing coaching that elevates individual craft and collective output
  • Serve as the primary creative partner to senior Client stakeholders, including marketing leadership and firm partners, presenting creative strategy and executions with confidence and clarity at executive level
  • Oversee the production of high-quality communications tailored for professional services audiences — from thought leadership campaigns and pitches to events and digital content
  • Champion and evolve Client's brand system, keeping it contemporary, distinctive, and appropriate for a regulated sector environment
  • Manage multiple concurrent projects across the portfolio, balancing hands-on creative contribution with leadership responsibilities and proactive problem-solving
  • Collaborate with OLIVER's wider creative and account leadership to identify opportunities to grow the studio's offering and deepen the Client relationship
  • Oversee studio-level production budgets — including cost estimation, supplier relationships, and spend reporting — ensuring financial performance aligns with Client and OLIVER expectations
  • Drive responsible integration of AI tools across studio workflows, setting quality standards and governance that preserve craft excellence while improving efficiency 

What you need to be great in this role: 

 

  • A strong portfolio of sophisticated brand and campaign work, with particular depth in B2B, corporate, or professional services environments
  • Expert-level understanding of brand systems — how to build, maintain, and evolve them within complex, regulated contexts
  • A track record of leading and developing creative teams, with a coaching approach that brings out the best in people at all levels
  • Experience presenting creative work to executive and partner-level audiences, with the presence and communication skills to hold a room and advocate for ideas with conviction
  • Deep craft knowledge across print and digital — typography, layout, art direction, and visual storytelling — with the ability to contribute hands-on when the work demands it
  • Proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign) and familiarity with Figma and contemporary design tooling
  • Experience managing studio-level or project-level production budgets, including supplier relationships and cost oversight
  • Experience integrating AI tools strategically across studio projects and operations, with the ability to set quality standards and governance at studio level
  • Clear understanding of where AI enhances creative output — and where human craft and judgement remain essential
  • Drives thoughtful AI adoption within the team, maintaining rigorous human oversight and mentoring others in responsible, effective use
  • Agentic approach to complex creative and business challenges: systematic, adaptive, and focused on outcomes

Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Why Deliveroo?

We're building the definitive online food company, transforming the way the world eats by making hyper-local food more convenient and accessible. We obsess about building the future of food, whilst using our network as a force for good. We're at the forefront of an industry, powered by our market-leading technology and unrivalled network to bring incredible convenience and selection to our customers.

Working at Deliveroo is the perfect environment to build a definitive career, motivated by impact. Firstly, the impact that working here will have on your development, allowing you to grow faster than you might elsewhere; secondly, the impact that you can have on Deliveroo, leaving your mark as we scale; and finally, being part of something bigger, through the impact that we make together in our marketplace and communities.


About the Role

We're hiring an engineer for the Storefront team to build the digital experiences behind merchants' own branded websites and apps. This is an opportunity to work on highly visible, customer-facing products while solving meaningful platform challenges.

 

What you'll do?

As a Software Engineer at Deliveroo, your individual work contributes to achieving goals in and across your team. While you will work with your team and you may lead projects, some of your work will contribute outside of your direct remit. You will report to managers and group leads and together deliver the results.

Technical Execution:

  • You will improve code structure, have an impact on architecture, and review code of any scope produced by your team.
  • You'll aim to simplify the maintenance and operation of production systems, visibility, operational readiness, and health of your team's systems.

Collaboration & Leadership:

  • As well as leading from the front regarding technical execution, you'll build relationships with other engineering teams and, identify collaboration opportunities.
  • You'll own larger pieces of work, assist with design and technical / implementation choices and influence the roadmap within your team.
  • You will take an active role in the hiring process and conducting engineering interviews. This will also extend to the current team where you will support the personal growth of colleagues, encouraging efficiency in their roles.

Expectations:

We want to emphasise that we don't expect you to meet all of the below but would love you to have experience in some of these areas.

  • Pride in readable, well-designed, well-tested software
  • Experience with Go and/or Python 
  • Experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL)
  • Experience with web architecture at scale (20krpm and above)
  •   Experience with "NoSQL" data backends and other (Redis, DynamoDB, ElasticSearch, Memcache)
  • Experience solving logistical problems with software

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, you'll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that's constantly evolving. We're food lovers, problem solvers, community organisers, proud parents, and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:

  • 🔧 Solve meaningful problems at real scale — Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.
  • 🌱 See your impact, fast — Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment.
  • 🧠 Grow through challenge and ownership — Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.
  • 🌎 A culture built for builders — High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.
  • 💰 Share in the success you help create — Competitive salary and equity options, so you're rewarded for the impact you make.

➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Check out our Tech Blog.

We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine—our interview typically includes 3-4 stages. Explore our Engineering Interview Guide here to help you feel confident at each stage.

 

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!


Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness.

Notre mission ⚖️

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.

Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.

Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.

Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.

Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.

Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.

Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.


Le contexte

Les cabinets d’avocats indépendants représentent le segment qui connaît la plus forte croissance chez Doctrine, avec une hausse de 50 % sur les 12 derniers mois.

Pour accompagner cette dynamique, tu joueras un rôle clé dans la fidélisation de nos clients et le développement de ton portefeuille. 

Nous recherchons un·e Account Manager (Retention Specialist) pour rejoindre notre équipe dédiée aux avocats indépendants.

Tu seras responsable d’un portefeuille de plus de 800 clients, avec une priorité : leur donner envie de rester chez Doctrine. Cela passe par des échanges réguliers, des démonstrations utiles à leur pratique et des négociations pour renouveler leur abonnement.
